record.title: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash-1017 open weights with claimed benchmark and runtime gains
record.summary: DeepSeek dated V4.1-Flash-1017 to October 17, 2026, reporting deployment to its web, app and API services. DeepSeek's official Hugging Face organization also hosts a distinct repository for the 1017 checkpoint under the MIT license, with about 510 GB of model files and a 1-million-token recommended context. The model card compares the new version with September's V4.1-Flash and reports gains on several agent and coding benchmarks, including DeepSWE v1.1 (74.2 to 77.0), NL2Repo-Bench (65.4 to 68.2) and Agents' Last Exam (31.8 to 35.4). These are provider-reported results; the linked technical report is the September report, not a 1017-specific report, and this activation did not independently evaluate the model.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: DeepSeek dated V4.1-Flash-1017 to 2026-10-17 and says the web/app models and API were updated to this version.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: An official DeepSeek Hugging Face repository exposes V4.1-Flash-1017 weights under the MIT license; the page lists approximately 510 GB of files and a 1M-token recommended context.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: DeepSeek reports higher benchmark scores for 1017 than for September's V4.1-Flash, including DeepSWE v1.1 74.2 to 77.0, NL2Repo-Bench 65.4 to 68.2 and Agents' Last Exam 31.8 to 35.4.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The release establishes independently reproduced capability improvements, lower cost, or lower runtime.

evidence_gaps.description: Obtain a 1017-specific technical report and detailed account of training or post-training changes.

Independently compare the 1017 and September checkpoints using identical benchmark versions, harnesses, prompts, tool settings, effort, sampling and output budgets; report raw outputs and uncertainty.
Measure quality, runtime, output-token use, peak memory and cost on stated hardware and serving settings.

brief.importance_rationale: If the released 1017 checkpoint's reported gains generalize, this is a very major open-model update: a widely inspectable MIT-licensed version of a very large multimodal model could materially affect access to capable coding and agent systems and the economics of open-model deployment. The score reflects consequence if true, not confidence; the benchmark and efficiency improvements are provider-reported, the checkpoint is about 510 GB, and no independent matched evaluation or realized cost result was reviewed.
limitations: Benchmark scores and the reported performance-cost Pareto improvement are provider claims; no independent evaluation was performed in this activation.
Benchmark names, versions, harnesses and task regimes differ across rows. Terminal-Bench 4.0 should not be compared directly with earlier Terminal-Bench 2.1 or 3.0 scores.
No 1017-specific technical report, training-change description, full evaluation protocol, raw results or uncertainty estimates were found in the inspected first-party materials.
The approximately 510 GB artifact is not a low-resource model; its public availability does not establish affordable or widely accessible self-hosting.
brief.summary: DeepSeek dated V4.1-Flash-1017 to October 17, 2026, reporting deployment to its web, app and API services. DeepSeek's official Hugging Face organization also hosts a distinct repository for the 1017 checkpoint under the MIT license, with about 510 GB of model files and a 1-million-token recommended context. The model card compares the new version with September's V4.1-Flash and reports gains on several agent and coding benchmarks, including DeepSWE v1.1 (74.2 to 77.0), NL2Repo-Bench (65.4 to 68.2) and Agents' Last Exam (31.8 to 35.4). These are provider-reported results; the linked technical report is the September report, not a 1017-specific report, and this activation did not independently evaluate the model.

technical.claimed_result: DeepSeek reports increased scores against the September V4.1-Flash on HLE text-only, Terminal-Bench 4.0, DeepSWE v1.1, ProgramBench, NL2Repo-Bench, Automation-Bench, Agents' Last Exam, Apex Bench and visual benchmarks; it also claims lower task time and output length. Same-version examples include DeepSWE v1.1 74.2 to 77.0, NL2Repo-Bench 65.4 to 68.2 and Agents' Last Exam 31.8 to 35.4.
technical.compute_or_cost: The official model repository lists about 510 GB of model files. DeepSeek claims lower task runtime and output length but publishes no absolute cost or independently measured runtime in the inspected update materials.
technical.demonstrated_result: The dated official changelog and a distinct official Hugging Face repository document the named version. The repository exposes model files under the MIT license. No independent evaluation was performed in this activation.
technical.implementation_status: A distinct official model repository is publicly available under MIT. DeepSeek says its web/app models and API use the 1017 revision; no independent endpoint-version check was made.
technical.mechanism: The 1017 checkpoint is described by DeepSeek as a minor weight update to V4.1-Flash. The official model card gives inference guidance and a 1M-token context recommendation. The inspected sources do not disclose the training changes behind the update.
technical.novelty: This is a dated weight-version release, separate from the September V4.1-Flash checkpoint. Its bounded novelty is the new public checkpoint and claimed gains, not a newly disclosed architecture.
technical.regime: First-party model release and benchmark report for a multimodal model with a listed artifact size of about 510 GB and 1M-token context recommendation. The repository's hosting and license are directly inspectable; the reported capability and cost differences are not independently established.
technical.reproducibility: Weights and inference guidance are available in the official repository. No 1017-specific technical report, full evaluation protocol, raw result artifact or independent matched reproduction was found; the model card's technical-report link points to the prior September release.
technical.strongest_baseline: The model card's comparison column for the September V4.1-Flash is the closest reported baseline. The evaluations remain provider-reported, and no matched independent run was inspected.

brief.title: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash-1017 open weights with claimed benchmark and runtime gains
brief.why_it_matters: A new openly available version of a very large multimodal model can change the capabilities available to researchers and developers and may shift open-model competition in coding and agent work. The release makes model weights and evaluation claims inspectable, while the model's approximately 510 GB repository implies substantial hardware requirements. The provider reports lower task time and output length, but no matched independent cost or runtime measurement is available here.
